messages:
alex: heads-up: after the routing rollout at 09:00 UTC a subset of SSE clients are flapping — they drop and immediately reconnect. console shows 200s for the initial reqs but the stream view shows short lived connections. no obvious quota spike. logs attached below. :eyes:

alex: example client log (trimmed):
```
2024-07-12T09:02:15Z INFO connect id=cli-42 session=opaque-7a2 status=200
2024-07-12T09:02:17Z WARN connection lost id=cli-42 reason=401_reauth
2024-07-12T09:02:17Z INFO reconnecting id=cli-42 session=opaque-9d3
```

alex: also running a curl shows keepalive still open on upstream but our proxy returned a 204-ish close chunk on the stream. not sure if auth TTL mismatch or route fallthrough. anyone seen similar after the route-policy swap?

maria: saw reports in telemetry too, small cohort. console metrics didn't have `resume_id` or `session_age` tags for those streams so grouping hides the churn. I think our new fallthrough path drops the auth cookie earlier. :thinking:

maria: quick query I ran: `sum by(route, status)(increase(streams_closed_total[5m]))` shows a bump on route=v2-fallback around the rollout window.

sam: repro steps? I can run a local canary. curious if this causes double-billing for token usage when client reconnects quickly.

alex: I reproduced by flipping the route locally. client reauth returns 401, client reconnects and gets a fresh session id -> two separate session counts. console still attributes both to same user but different session tags. billing could count both as separate calls.

irene: that could ring the billing alarm. we have dedupe for short-lived reconnects but it relies on `resume-id` header present in request. if the proxy path strips it, dedupe fails. we should validate whether fallthrough removes headers.

deploy-bot: deploy 5812339800 by @maria: routing-config v2 -> v2-fallback (canary 10%).

jamie: proposal: roll back fallback routing for the canary while we add resume-id passthrough and session_age tagging. rollback is quick and minimizes user impact. :+1:

maria: agreed. also proposing a tiny telemetry change: emit `stream_resume` metric with label `resume_present=true|false` and `resume_id` as a tag (hashed) so console can show counts of reconnects with missing resume. small code diff below.

maria: config diff (pseudo):
```
- metrics.emit("stream_closed", { route })
+ metrics.emit("stream_closed", { route, resume_present: !!headers['x-resume-id'], resume_hash: hash(headers['x-resume-id'] || '') })
```

sam: I can run a 5% canary with the header passthrough and telemetry. we should also bump the console to display `last_resume_hash` in the stream timeline so SREs can triage faster.

jamie: can we avoid exposing `resume_id` raw in the console? hashing is fine. UX tweak to show `resume=✓` or `resume=missing` and an obfuscated id. product ping? @matt-product can you prioritize a small column?

alex: @matt-product fyi this is affecting a small set of customers; UX tweak will speed triage. otherwise i'm inclined to rollback the canary in 15m if sam sees production traffic still flapping.

irene: also check billing pipeline for the dedupe TTL window. if dedupe window is 2s and clients reconnect in <1s we should be fine, but current reconnects look ~200-500ms. might need to extend dedupe window to 1s for rollouts.

maria: test plan: 1) enable header passthrough on fallback path, 2) emit resume_present metric, 3) run 5% canary for 30m, 4) monitor `streams_closed_total` and `billing_dedupe_hits`. sam volunteered to run it.

sam: starting canary now (5%). will post numbers in 10m. :rocket:

alex: thanks. if anyone spots `x-resume-id` being stripped by nginx/proxy, post the exact config line. we need to ensure `proxy_set_header` keeps it.

maria: note: edge proxy had `proxy_pass_request_headers on;` but we found `proxy_hide_header X-Resume-Id;` in one branch (oops). will open a PR to remove that.

jamie: if we do rollback, also add a console banner explaining potential duplicate session counts during the rollout window so CS doesn't freak out.

alex: good call. i'll draft a short banner and cc @sales-ops.

sam: canary traffic looks cleaner already, resume_present true went from 12% -> 86% in the canary cohort and closed_stream rate down 60% in 8m. will keep monitoring.

alex: great. once canary holds for 30m we can rollout fix to 100% and update billing dedupe TTL if needed. thanks all. :raised_hands:
